new_value: Unified on OSCORE_ERR_INVALID_PARAM for the NULL-options-with-content condition. Majority convention ruled: protect_response (all NULL outputs -> INVALID_PARAM) and unprotect_response (NULL options/payload with content -> INVALID_PARAM) already treat NULL buffers as caller-contract violations while reserving BUFFER_TOO_SMALL for insufficient capacity, so oscore_unprotect_request (oscore_protect.c) was the odd one out and is the single site changed: the previously merged condition was split so NULL options (opt_out_len>0) or NULL payload (pay_len>0) now return OSCORE_ERR_INVALID_PARAM while capacity shortfalls keep OSCORE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, exactly mirroring the response sibling's structure. Both header docs updated to state the split explicitly (unprotect_request and unprotect_response now document NULL-with-content -> INVALID_PARAM, capacity -> BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, removed size-query mode). No in-tree caller passes NULL with content (coap_oscore.c:208 passes real buffers), so no caller behavior changes. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra across the 4 Kconfig combos (PT_MAX 256/2048 x MAX_CONTEXTS 8/32) clean; host harness exercises both capacity-failure paths and NULL sentinel checks remain green (rr_harness + margin_harness, ASan+UBSan).
